transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Sara Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Martinez (Redwood SE); Aisha Rahman (Head of Product, LumenPath); Tom Keller (Platform Eng); Priya Nair (ML Eng)

Summary: quick PLG/self-serve discovery — LumenPath is prototyping an assistant for enterprise analytics. Primary ask: how fast can they get first token (time-to-first-token), what free credits/quickstart help, and when to move to Dedicated or Private for data controls.

Topics covered: quickstart credits; console experience; Curl/SDK flow to first token; Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs; security (SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS); basic cost/latency expectations; next steps and owners.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto-generated transcription — some mis-words expected) ---
[00:00] Sara Chen (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Sara, AE on the infra team, and Diego is our solutions engineer. how are folks doing?
[00:08] Aisha Rahman (LumenPath): good, thanks. excited to get into this. we want to validate a quick POC — basically how fast our devs can go from zero to first token using the self-serve redwood api.
[00:16] Diego Martinez (Redwood SE): awesome, focusing on time-to-first-token is exactly where PLG shines. i'll run through the quickstart and then we can talk about capacity and security.
[00:25] Tom Keller (LumenPath): quick note: we are currently on internal infra in aws, everything in a VPC, with strict egress rules. likely will need V P C peering or private deployment later.
[00:34] Priya Nair (LumenPath): our SLO for the assistant is p95 latency <400ms for short prompts — that's one of our constraints.
[00:42] Diego Martinez (Redwood SE): perfect — for hosted quickstarts we can usually get devs from signup to first token in under 20 minutes. free credits speed that along. Dedicated is more about predictable throughput — so that's a follow-up.
[00:55] Aisha: when you say "first token in 20 minutes" what's included? sign-up, key, sample request?
[01:02] Sara: yes — sign up, confirm email, console quickstart, copy API key, run curl or SDK example. Diego: can you show the curl snippet?
[01:10] Diego: sure — typical flow is: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"rw-base-1","input":"Hello"}'  — that returns completions. sometimes the transcript generator munges urls in auto transcribe, but the idea is simple.
[01:26] Tom: will the key be limited by credits? we need to ensure we don't accidentally spin large bills.
[01:32] Sara: yes, quickstart credits are applied to the account and you can cap usage via rate limits and quotas in the console. we'll issue $30 in credits for this POC.
[01:39] Aisha: ok great. next, security: we need SOC2 reports, network diagrams, SAML/SSO + SCIM. is that available in your enterprise pack?
[01:47] Sara: yes — we have SOC2 Type II reports and an enterprise security packet. i'll share the pdf and a network diagram template. we also support SAML, SCIM provisioning, and KMS integrations.
[01:56] Priya: when you say KMS integrations — can we bring our own key for the private deployment?
[02:02] Diego: for Private deployments yes — customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported. for Hosted, encrypted at rest is standard but BYOK is offered via dedicated or private contract.
[02:11] Aisha: timeline — if we sign up and do quickstart, how long until we can put a small app in front of internal users? 1 week?
[02:18] Diego: for a PLG self-serve quickstart, prototype in a day or two is common. for production with SSO and dedicated capacity, plan for 4–6 weeks depending on procurement.
[02:27] Tom: procurement question — we sometimes need to show vendor compliance docs earlier. can you push SOC2 and a network diagram now?
[02:34] Sara: yes — i'll attach them; action item for me.
[02:36] 
[05:05] (conversation skips to infra specifics)
[05:05] Tom: about VPC peering — if we do hosted, are there options for private egress or virtual appliance?
[05:13] Diego: hosted supports private egress via partner peering in some regions; otherwise Dedicated or Private gives full V P C control. sometimes the words "VPC" transcribe as separate letters in the auto text.
[05:23] Priya: ok on latency — do you have benchmarks for small LLMs at sequence lengths ~128? we care about p95 on short requests.
[05:30] Diego: we have perf profiles — i'll send a short spreadsheet. rough numbers: hosted rw-base at 1 request concurrency p95 ~ 220ms on our optimized GPU runtime; with batching at high concurrency you get better throughput but higher tail latency if you set big batch windows.
[05:48] Aisha: what's the advice for our use case — low latency for interactive queries vs cost?
[05:53] Diego: tradeoff is batching and quantization. for interactive <400ms we recommend single-instance low-batch config or small batch windows and use our latency-first kernel selection. for cost-sensitive ingestion you can enable batching and larger batch windows. also prefix/K V cache helps for repeated context. (auto transcript sometimes shows K V as K V cash).
[06:11] Tom: any restrictions on model variants when moving to Dedicated? can we pin model versions?
[06:16] Sara: yes — Dedicated lets you pin model versions and control rollouts; you can also run canary traffic.
[06:21] Priya: curious about time-to-first-token for Private on-prem — that seems like more work. what's a rough lead time?
[06:27] Diego: Private is heavier: packaging, network validation, security review — 6–12 weeks typical. Hosted quickstart is the fastest for experimentation.
[06:34] Aisha: for the POC, we just want to validate UX and hallucination rates on our prompt set, not ship to customers. so hosted quickstart + sample eval harness should do.
[06:43] Diego: we can provide an eval harness and a small demo repo that runs A/Bs and regression checks, ties to quality monitoring.
[06:50] 
[12:00] (mid-call clarifications, some crosstalk)
[12:01] Priya: one more technical — do you allow streaming completions and function/tool calls? we want streaming for our assistant.
[12:07] Diego: yes — streaming, function calling, structured output are supported. streaming behavior depends on client libs; for curl short polling works but SDKs have nicer streaming.
[12:18] Aisha: are embeddings separate billing? we'll likely use embeddings for vector search in the product.
[12:23] Sara: embeddings are billed per unit; we'll share pricing sheet. quickstart credits apply across features.
[12:29] Tom: how do you handle data retention and logs for hosted accounts? we need audit logs for internal compliance.
[12:35] Sara: hosted provides audit logs and configurable retention; for enterprise we expose token-level tracing in the console and you can set retention windows. Private gives you full control.
[12:44] 
[18:10] (discussion about conversion path and cost)
[18:10] Aisha: if we like the POC we will likely push for Dedicated — what triggers that? raw throughput or security?
[18:16] Diego: typically it's predictable throughput needs, strict data controls, or cost targets that Dedicated meets better. also long-term we help right-size GPU pools and autoscaling policies.
[18:25] Aisha: any gotchas with autoscaling and warmup time?
[18:29] Diego: yes — cold start can add to latency; we do warm pools and burst cap. we'll size pools and can pre-warm KV caches.
[18:36] Tom: can you show the console's quickstart flow?
[18:39] Diego: (screenshare reference) from the console you can create an API key, view quickstart snippets (curl, python sdk), and toggle quotas. i'll share a recording and a link: https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart (note: auto transcript sometimes mangles urls).
[18:58] Priya: will you generate a small sample app repo we can fork?
[19:02] Sara: yes — we'll drop a repo with the minimal stack (react + backend) demonstrating streaming and function calls.
[19:10] 
[25:00] (procurement & compliance)
[25:00] Tom: procurement will need terms sheet and a rudimentary SOW if we move to Dedicated. is there a standard template?
[25:06] Sara: yes, we have an MSA and SOW templates. for Dedicated we typically outline commit levels and SLA.
[25:12] Aisha: on billing — do you support invoicing?
[25:15] Sara: enterprise invoicing, yes. self-serve is card by default.
[25:20] 
[30:00] (wrap up and recap)
[30:00] Sara: recap — we'll provision $30 quickstart credits and send quickstart link and sample repo. Diego will run a latency/cost estimate for a 2k qps scenario and share perf sheet. Tom to share traffic/profile dump. we'll send SOC2 and network diagram.
[30:15] Aisha: that works. can we get all that by Friday?
[30:19] Sara: yes — i'll send credits and docs by Thursday EOD, Diego's estimate by next Tuesday.
[30:25] Priya: i'll start the onboarding checklist on our side.
[30:28] 
[36:00] (closing pleasantries)
[36:00] Sara: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and next meeting invite.
[36:06] Aisha: thanks, appreciate it.
[36:09] Tom: thanks.
